fatal_errors: The proposed material is not the target AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic HEA with FCC and B2 phases.
The stated (CoNi)50(TiZrHf)50 structure is incorrectly described as FCC; the cited evidence identifies it as a single-phase B2 high-entropy intermetallic.
Composition adjustment and mechanical testing across homologous temperatures do not reconstruct the required intermediate-temperature aging treatment at approximately 600°C and 750°C.
None of the cited evidence demonstrates a non-monotonic ductile-brittle-ductile transition.
The proposed amorphization and dynamic-hardening mechanism is unrelated to the target coupling of enhanced L12 ordering, jagged B2/FCC phase boundaries, planar slip, and crack initiation.
The falsification rule merely restates the desired outcome and does not define a measurable brittle-window criterion or distinguish the proposed mechanism from alternatives.
explanation: The hypothesis only matches the broad theme that a compositionally complex alloy might show unusual ductility behavior. It substitutes unrelated B2 intermetallic, refractory-HEA, and hydrogen-resistant MEA literature for the relevant eutectic AlCoCrFeNi2.1 system. It misses the as-cast FCC+B2 initial state, the 550–750°C aging window, maximum embrittlement near 600°C, recovery near 750°C, enhanced L12 ordering, jagged phase-boundary morphology, elevated APBE and planar slip, and ductile transition zones at higher aging temperature. The predicted outcome invokes a ductile-brittle-ductile transition but does not actually specify or support an intermediate brittle state; instead, it emphasizes plasticity at both room and high temperatures. The proposed experiments could characterize general deformation but would not directly test crack initiation at jagged phase-boundary tips, ordering-dependent dislocation behavior, or exclusion of impurity-segregation-mediated temper embrittlement.
